title: She Cleared 4.25 Metres and Broke a Record That Was Only Days Old. Indian Women's Pole Vault Has Arrived.
excerpt: Karnataka's Sindhushree G set a new national record at the Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar, beating rival Baranica Elangovan's mark and qualifying for the Asian Games — part of a week that saw national records fall across five disciplines.
body:
Karnataka's Sindhushree G rewrote the national record books in women's pole vault at the 65th National Inter-State Senior Athletics Championships in Bhubaneswar, clearing 4.25 metres to claim gold and a berth at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.

The 26-year-old's leap surpassed the previous national record of 4.23 metres set recently by Baranica Elangovan, who finished second at 4.20 metres. It also shattered the meet record of 4.10 metres that Pavithra Venkatesh had held since 2023. All three medallists — Sindhushree, Baranica, and bronze winner Nitika Akare of Madhya Pradesh, who cleared the Asian Games qualifying mark of 4.10 metres — are now in contention for the Indian squad heading to Japan in September.

"I had trained hard, but the national record was a bonus," a jubilant Sindhushree said after the competition at Kalinga Stadium. "I was mentally prepared to book an Asian Games berth."

## A Record-Breaking Week in Bhubaneswar

Sindhushree's performance was the highlight of a Day 2 that saw seventeen athletes clear qualification standards for the Asian Games across multiple disciplines. It also capped an extraordinary week for Indian athletics in Bhubaneswar, where national records have fallen like dominos.



> **""I had trained hard, but the national record was a bonus," a jubilant Sindhushree said after the competition at Kalinga Stadium."**


On Day 1, eighteen-year-old Anushka Yadav from Uttar Pradesh hurled the hammer to 67.02 metres — obliterating Sarita A Singh's nine-year-old national record of 65.25 metres — while Dev Meena of Madhya Pradesh cleared 5.46 metres to claim the men's pole vault record outright. On the same evening, Jyothi Yarraji ran 12.99 seconds in the 100 metres hurdles, dipping below 13 seconds for the first time since an injury sidelined her for exactly twelve months.

By Day 3, six men's triple jumpers had all cleared the Asian Games qualifying mark, and Haryana's Seema threw the discus 59.73 metres — another dominant performance well beyond the 55.48-metre standard.

## The Quiet Depth Behind the Headlines

What makes this week's results striking is not just the records but the depth beneath them. In women's pole vault alone, three athletes cleared the Asian Games qualifying height in the same competition — a first for the event. Until recently, Indian women's pole vault was a peripheral discipline. The fact that Sindhushree and Baranica are now trading national records back and forth suggests a genuine talent cluster rather than a single isolated breakthrough.

Similar depth is emerging in women's shot put, where all three medallists — Manpreet Kaur (17.75 metres), Srishti Vig (16.96 metres), and Krishna Jayashankar (16.69 metres) — surpassed the Asian Games qualifying mark of 16.25 metres. Harita Bhadra's gold in the women's 200 metres (23.14 seconds) and Gowthami Jayaraman's 800-metre victory (2:04.17) showed similar class.

The Athletics Federation of India's selection committee will finalise the Asian Games-bound contingent after the championships conclude, but the depth on display suggests India will field a significantly stronger women's contingent than in previous editions.

## Why the Diaspora Should Pay Attention

The 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, which begin on 19 September, will be the first major multi-sport event to test India's post-Olympic athletics ambitions. For the Indian diaspora — particularly in North America and Europe, where athletics is followed far more closely than on the subcontinent — these qualifying competitions offer a preview of what India might bring to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

The men's and women's pole vault stories carry particular resonance. The national record in men's pole vault has been improved five times in under two years. On the women's side, the Sindhushree-Baranica rivalry now mirrors the kind of domestic competition that historically produced breakthroughs in sprints and throws.

India will also be represented at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, where athletes like Mirabai Chanu and the newly qualified contingent from Bhubaneswar will compete in front of a substantial British Indian audience. For those following from abroad, Bhubaneswar's Kalinga Stadium has quietly become the incubator — the place where the next generation of Indian athletics talent announces itself before stepping onto the global stage.

**Sources:** Athletics Federation of India (AFI) press releases; IANS reporting from Bhubaneswar; Revsportz; Yardbarker
